QuestionStmt.S: The surface energy of a liquid drop is '$V$'. It is sprayed into 1000 equal droplets. The surface energy of all the droplets is

Solution.S:
Let $R$ be the radius of the bigger drop and $r$ be the radius of each small droplet.

Mass is conserved, so:

$$\rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = \rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \times 1000$$

$$R^3 = 1000 r^3$$

$$R = 10r$$

Surface energy of the bigger drop:

$$V = (4\pi R^2) T$$

Total surface energy of all 1000 small droplets:

$$V' = n \times (4\pi r^2) T = 1000 \times 4\pi r^2 \times T$$

Substitute $r = \frac{R}{10}$:

$$V' = 1000 \times 4\pi \left(\frac{R}{10}\right)^2 \times T = \frac{1000}{100} \times 4\pi R^2 T = 10 \times V$$

Thus the total surface energy of all droplets is $10V$, which corresponds to option B.
